newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end steady/up as short covering eases.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end steady/up as short covering eases.

text.p: Short covering that boosted CME lumber futures up from initial losses waned late and prices ended only steady to slightly higher, traders said.
Lumber closed unchanged to $2.00 higher with May unchanged at $359.50 and July up $2.00 at $357.50 per tbf.

Initial carryover selling from Wednesday's limit losses lacked followthrough after filling a chart point and futures ran up for net gains on short covering. But prices slowly worked back as concern continued over the slow pace of cash trade and expectations that cash spruce may be quoted lower again Friday, traders said.
"Demand for wood has remained slow and spruce could lose a few more dollars," one trader said.
